attempts.text:
The prognosis is influenced by several documented factors. Preoperative PSA was 4.7, and the surgical pathology revealed a Gleason 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2) with positive surgical margins and extraprostatic extension, which are concerning features. Conversely, the seminal vesicles were not invaded, and lymphovascular invasion was absent. The biopsy showed a Gleason 3+3 (ISUP grade group 1), which differs from the prostatectomy specimen. The absence of lymph node removal and the lack of documented nodal sampling widen the uncertainty regarding nodal status.

The primary driver for prognosis is the positive margins and T3a stage. Countervailing factors include the absence of seminal vesicle invasion and lymphovascular invasion. Information that would significantly revise this prognosis includes postoperative PSA levels and its subsequent trajectory. Missing postoperative PSA or follow-up data currently prevents a definitive assessment of recurrence risk. The expected follow-up without an event is 62.79 months.

The patient underwent a robot-assisted radical prostatectomy with a pathological stage of pT3a, positive surgical margins, and no invasion of the seminal vesicles. The surgical specimen demonstrated a Gleason 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2). Biopsy findings showed a Gleason 3+3 (ISUP grade group 1). The absence of lymph nodes removed is noted, which widens uncertainty as nodal sampling was not performed. The preoperative PSA was 4.7.

Factors driving prognosis include the positive surgical margins and the higher Gleason grade identified post-surgery. Countervailing findings include the absence of lymphovascular invasion and the lack of seminal vesicle invasion. The difference between the biopsy grade (Gleason 3+3) and the prostatectomy grade (Gleason 3+4) is a point of consideration. Missing postoperative PSA or follow-up information would revise the prognosis and its subsequent trajectory. The current heuristic horizon suggests a time to recurrence of 62.79 months.
